data.cause: The primary resolver on dns1.lan rate-limits the whole LAN to a single 20 q/s bucket (ratelimit_subnet_len_ipv4: 24 over 10.20.0.0/24), so brief traffic bursts make it drop queries several times a day; the clients' fallback server gw.lan can't cover for it because its unbound DNS-rebinding protection (private-address: 10.0.0.0/8) strips the RFC1918 answer for .lan names, so getaddrinfo sees NXDOMAIN-like empty answers until the burst passes.
evidence: journalctl -u primary-dns on dns1.lan shows repeated 'ratelimit: 10.20.0.0/24 exceeded 20 q/s, dropping N queries' episodes at 02:14, 09:41 and 13:02, each ending within ~30s — matching alerts that clear in a minute or two
cat /opt/primary-dns/config.yaml shows ratelimit: 20 with ratelimit_subnet_len_ipv4: 24, i.e. one shared bucket for all clients in 10.20.0.0/24
dig @10.20.0.3 nas.lan from mon.lan returns NOERROR with nas.lan A 10.20.0.50 (TTL 10), so normal lookups succeed via the first server
dig @10.20.0.1 nas.lan from mon.lan returns NOERROR with ANSWER: 0 — the fallback server yields no address for local names

cat /var/unbound/unbound.conf on gw.lan shows DNS rebinding protection 'private-address: 10.0.0.0/8' applied to forwarded .lan answers, while internet names (public addresses) are unaffected — matching 'internet names not affected'
data.recommendation: Fix the rate limiting on dns1.lan's primary-dns: raise the ratelimit well above the LAN's burst rate and/or set ratelimit_subnet_len_ipv4 to 32 so each client gets its own bucket instead of the whole /24 sharing 20 q/s. Additionally, make the fallback usable for local names on gw.lan's unbound by exempting the .lan zone from private-address filtering (e.g. declare lan. as a local zone or use private-address: except for it). The smallest effective change is raising/widening the rate-limit scope on dns1; the gw.lan exemption makes the second configured resolver actually helpful for .lan.
